title: NimbusFin Dedicated Capacity Discovery
next_steps: Share Dedicated pricing SKU and estimated TCO
Schedule technical deep-dive to run a 1h benchmark on their sample workload next week
action_items: Jordan Park: Share Dedicated pricing spreadsheet and committed capacity options (due: 2025-10-09)
Leah Martinez: Prep benchmark plan and list of required sample inputs for the 1h run (due: 2025-10-10)
Priya Nair: Provide sample inference workload (prompts + typical seq lengths) and SLO targets (due: 2025-10-09)
summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated GPU capacity for latency-sensitive financial inference workloads. Customer needs isolation for PII/regulatory reasons, predictable throughput for peak trading windows, and burst capability for irregular spikes. Key concerns: cost predictability, data residency, SOC2 and KMS integration, and ability to scale from dev to prod without re-architecting. Agreed next steps: share pricing, security docs, and schedule a benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting: 2025-10-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Leah Martinez (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO - NimbusFin), Priya Nair (ML Engineer), Samir Gupta (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes, we'll do intros quick and then dig into your workload and dedicated capacity needs.
[00:15] Marcus: great, thanks. quick intro from our side, i'm marcus, cto; priya handles ml ops and infra, samir is our infra and security lead.
[00:30] Jordan: awesome. leah from my team is our solutions engineer, she'll go deep on perf and capacity. leah over to you.
[00:40] Leah: thanks jordan. hi all, wanted to start by understanding current infra — are you on cloud GPUs today, or a mix? whats the model footprint?
[00:52] Priya: we run a mix — batch training in gcp, but inference is in prod on a mix of smaller gpus in-house and some aws instances. we have two main models: a customer-service triage model (7B quantized) and a risk-scoring model that's like a 13B variant. latency target for risk scoring is sub-150ms p95 token for our typical 128 token requests.
[01:20] Samir: and importantly we need isolation/data separation for regulatory and audit reasons, some of the data is regulated financial PII and we can't have it cross-tenant on shared infra.
[01:35] Jordan: right, dedicated looks like the fit then — reserved GPU pools with isolation. curious what your expected steady-state QPS/throughput is and how much burst you want?
[01:48] Marcus: steady ci for trading hours is about 70 qps across the risk scorer endpoints, but we have big spikes at market open where it can go up 5x for a few minutes. we also want predictable tail latency.
[02:05] Leah: ok that helps. how do you think about batching and latency; are you flexible on batching to reduce cost or is latency inviolable?
[02:15] Priya: for risk scoring latency is pretty strict, we can accept micro-batching up to maybe 4 requests if p95 stays under target, but not large batching. we also want prefix caching for repeated customer prompts on the triage model.
[02:31] Jordan: and for dedicated we support configurable autoscaling plus burst pools — you can reserve baseline GPUs and have a burst tier that allows short-term capacity with pricing tradeoffs.
[02:42] Samir: how is the burst capacity billed and is data isolated in the burst tier? we can't have data touching shared multi-tenant nodes unless it's encrypted and ephemeral.
[02:55] Leah: good question. burst nodes can be configured as private within your dedicated pool; if you opt into Redwood's shared burst capacity it'll be multi-tenant and the usual network-level isolation applies but not the same physical isolation. for regulated workloads we recommend dedicated burst nodes or using Private deployment.
[03:15] Marcus: hmm, what's the difference between Dedicated + private burst nodes vs Private deployment?
[03:23] Leah: Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools in our infrastructure but logically isolated for your account. Private is a customer-managed control plane — V P C peering or on-prem — so you get full network control and customer-managed keys. Dedicated with private nodes gives you physical isolation but still uses Redwood control plane; Private gives more control, higher ops overhead.
[03:45] Priya: for us a big question is key management — we need KMS integration for our encryption keys and HSM support ideally. can we integrate our existing cloud KMS?
[03:55] Jordan: yes, for Dedicated we support customer KMS integration for model artifacts and logs; Private supports HSM/KMS in customer account as well. we'll share the security integration doc.
[04:05] Samir: and audit logs? retention? we need 12 months of immutable logs for compliance.
[04:12] Leah: Redwood Console can export audit logs and we have longer retention add-ons. we'll include the retention options in the pack.
[04:20] Marcus: re: scale — how quickly can dedicated autoscale? our traffic is spiky.
[04:27] Leah: autoscaling reaction time depends on scaling policy and pre-warmed capacity. we recommend keeping baseline to cover p95 steady-state and use burst pool for spikes. for very tight tail latency we do warm pools and pre-warmed KV cache which reduces cold-start tok latency.
[04:45] Priya: what about model variants — we sometimes run 13b quant on weekdays and fall back to smaller for cost. can we set routing policies?
[04:55] Jordan: yes, we support smart routing by policy (latency, cost, region). you can set fallbacks to a quantized 13b or 7b depending on SLO breaches.
[05:05] Marcus: training/serving parity question — if we train and quantize models in house, can we bring them and Redwood serve them as-is?
[05:13] Leah: absolutely, we onboard customer models; we do some compatibility checks and might recommend quantization/compilation profiles. we also run a small perf validation.
[05:25] Samir: curious about networking — V P C peering, private endpoints, static egress IPs for allowlisting?
[05:33] Jordan: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link-like endpoints; static egress IPs are available for Dedicated Tenants. if you need on-prem we'll discuss Private.
[05:44] Priya: any restrictions on sequence lengths or token limits that affect kernel selection? we get variable seq lengths from 32 up to 512.
[05:54] Leah: kernel selection is adaptive; long sequences cost more, and our runtime picks optimized kernels and batching strategies. we'll want your seq distribution to size GPU memory needs.
[06:05] Marcus: what's the typical GPU types you run for dedicated? a100? h100?
[06:12] Jordan: we offer a mix — A100 for stable workloads, H100 for high throughput/large context. pricing differs. for quantized 13b many customers run on A100s with 80GB or optimized h100 for best latency.
[06:28] Samir: and how do we handle tenant isolation at kernel level — i mean, we need to be able to prove there's no cross-tenant data leakage.
[06:38] Leah: at Dedicated we provide isolated pools and we also provide auditability — logs and job-level metadata. for higher assurance we recommend Private with customer-controlled KMS and network.
[06:50] Marcus: data residency — we require that tokens and logs for EU customers remain in eu-region. can Dedicated guarantee region pinning?
[06:58] Jordan: yes, you can pin dedicated pools to regions; we have EU regions that satisfy data residency constraints. we'll list available regions in the follow-up.
[07:08] Priya: can we do a pilot with a small committed pool and then scale to larger reserved capacity? how's the contract?
[07:16] Jordan: we have flexible ramp options — short-term pilot credits and then monthly reserved capacity with discounts for annual commits. pilot can run on Dedicated trial nodes or Private trial depending on isolation needs.
[07:28] Marcus: cost math — curious about per-token vs per-GPU reserved cost. we'll need an estimate for our 70 qps steady state with spikes.
[07:38] Leah: we'll model it in the pricing sheet; typical levers are batch size, KV caching, and quantization. we'll run your workload in a benchmark to produce cost per inference and suggested pool sizes.
[07:52] Samir: action items we need: security docs, KMS integration reference, pricing, and a bench plan.
[08:00] Jordan: yes we'll do that.
[08:05] Leah: quick perf deep-dive question — do you store any user-specific cache that needs to be persisted per-tenant?
[08:12] Priya: yes we have some prefix cache keys per customer, we'd like persistent KV cache that is private to our account.
[08:20] Leah: Dedicated supports per-tenant KV cache, and you can control TTLs. that helps reduce cost for repeated prefixes.
[08:30] Marcus: what about multi-model routing and canary rollouts? we run model updates frequently and need A/B and canary.
[08:40] Jordan: Console supports rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback rules. we can do traffic splits by model version.
[08:49] Priya: latency SLO enforcement — can the runtime enforce per-route SLOs and trigger fallback automatically?
[08:56] Leah: yes, you can author policies that monitor p95 and trigger a fallback to a cheaper variant or route to a warm pool.
[09:05] Marcus: ok, timeline — we're aiming to have a pilot before end of q4 and a production migration in q1.
[09:13] Jordan: that's doable, we'll aim to get pricing and security docs to you in 48 hours and schedule the benchmark for next week.
[09:22] Samir: one more — SLA and uptime requirements; finance ops needs to know the SLOs for trading hours.
[09:30] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA options; we'll include the SLA tiers in the follow-up.
[09:36] Priya: can we do a short technical deep-dive with your infra team to confirm pre-warming strategies and the caching behavior?
[09:44] Leah: absolutely, we'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive; we'll bring ops and runtime engineers.
[09:52] Jordan: wrap-up — recap next steps and owners. we'll send pricing, security + KMS docs, region availability, and bench plan. schedule tech deep-dive and the 1h benchmark. thanks everyone.
[10:05] Marcus: thanks all.

Notes: transcript contains small ASR errors in product names (eg V P C sometimes spelled out), and occasional timestamps approximated.
